## Americas Gold and Silver Reports Financial Results for Q3 2026 Following Record Quarterly Silver Production Driven by Strong Operational Results at Cosalá


**TORONTO, ONTARIO** - November 13, 2026 – Americas Gold and Silver Corporation (TSX: USA) (NYSE American: USAS) (“Americas” or the “Company”) a North American producer of silver and other critical minerals supporting the growth of artificial intelligence (“AI”), electrification, national security, and advanced manufacturing, reports consolidated financial and operational results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


*This earnings release should be read in conjunction with the Company’s Management’s Discussion and Analysis, Financial Statements and Notes to Financial Statements for the corresponding period, which have been posted on the Americas Gold and Silver Corporation SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca, and on its EDGAR profile at www.sec.gov, and which are also available on the Company’s website at www.americas-gold.com. All figures are in U.S. dollars unless otherwise noted.*


**Highlights**


- **Record quarterly silver production and sales** driven by strong operational performance from Cosalá Operations and solid progress recovering from temporary production interruptions at the Galena complex during the prior quarter.


- Consolidated silver production of 800,458 ounces, a Company record, was realized during the quarter (a 5% increase compared to Q3-2025), or 936,870 silver equivalent ounces\[1\] , including approximately 965,000 pounds of lead, 918,000 pounds of copper and 101,000 pounds of antimony.
- Consolidated YTD-2026 silver production was approximately 2.3 million ounces (a 19% increase compared to YTD-2025), including approximately 5.2 million pounds of lead, 2.7 million pounds of copper, and 335,000 pounds of antimony.
- The Company remains on track to achieve the low end of existing full-year production guidance of 3.2 to 3.6 million silver ounces and the high end of AISC guidance range of $30 to $35 per ounce sold.


- **Consolidated net revenue increased to $51.4 million for Q3-2026** , or a 68% increase compared to $30.6 million for Q3-2025, primarily as a result of higher realized prices and higher production.


- YTD-2026 revenues of $165.5 million increased by 104% compared to YTD-2025 revenues of $81.1 million.


- **Exceptional operational performance at Cosalá,** delivering 415,879 ounces of silver during the quarter which represents a 28% year-over-year increase when compared to Q3-2025, driven by higher grades.


- Strong production was driven by higher silver grades across fewer tonnes as the Company enters the heart of the orebody at EC120, its flagship operation at Cosalá.


- **Achieved some of the best grade-widths drilled to date at the Cosalá operations** , including high-grade drill results of 654.7 g/t Ag, 1.5% Cu over 20.5 meters and 409.3 g/t Ag, 0.8% Cu over 14.1 meters (see Americas news release dated September 17, 2026 for further details).


- The assay results were part of infill and step-out drilling conducted in 1H 2026 at Cosalá’s San Rafael Upper, 120 Upper and 120 Lower deposits with multiple holes at all three zones returning substantially higher silver grades than the currently modeled Mineral Resource. These results demonstrate upside potential to the future mine plan as they were not included in the Company’s 2025 Mineral Resource and Mineral Reserve estimates (see Americas news release dated March 30, 2026), and will be considered in future updates to the Mineral Resource estimate.


- **Significant new high-grade Ag-Cu-Pb-Sb drill results at the Galena Complex** from the Company’s largest ever exploration and Mineral Resource conversion drilling program, as well as a significant new vein discovery at the Galena Mine on the operating 49 level (49-817 intersecting 1.2m of 1,061 g/t Ag, 0.7% Cu and 0.6% Sb – see Americas news release dated September 18, 2026 for further details). The new discovery is not only high grade, but also close to minimum mining widths required for the ongoing transition to long hole stoping.


- Assay results returned infill drill intercepts that are regularly intersecting higher silver grades than the currently modeled Mineral Resource. These results represent potential upside the future mine plan as they were not included in the Company’s 2025 Mineral Resource and Mineral Reserve estimates (see Americas news release dated March 30, 2026) and will be considered in future updates to the Mineral Resource estimate.


- **Named to 2026 TSX30TM** in the Toronto Stock Exchange’s (“TSX”) annual ranking of the 30 top-performing companies based on dividend-adjusted share price performance over a three-year period.


- The Company ranked 24th on the 2026 TSX30™, delivering a 477% increase in share price over the three-year period ended June 30, 2026, and generating CAD$2.2 billion in market capitalization growth on the TSX.


- **Published Americas’ Inaugural Corporate Sustainability Report** on October 13, 2026. The 2025 Sustainability Report is an important milestone in the growth of the Company as it outlines foundations of a comprehensive sustainability strategy that serves as a cornerstone of the aggressive growth plan by integrating key environmental, social, and governance factors into risk management systems, alongside key metrics for internal monitoring and external reporting.
- **Cash and cash equivalents balance of $63.3 million, available liquidity of $113 million** and working capital1 of $23.1 million as of September 30, 2026, in line with expectations as the Company continues to deploy capital into its consolidated revitalization and growth plans. An additional $50 million is available to the Company upon satisfaction of certain conditions from its existing $100 million Term Loan Facility, providing the Company with available liquidity of $113 million.
- **Cost of sales per silver equivalent ounce sold1, cash costs1 and all-in sustaining costs1 per silver ounce sold** averaged $31.68, $29.66 and $42.94, respectively, in Q3-2026.


- For YTD-2026, cost of sales per silver equivalent ounce sold, cash costs and all-in sustaining costs (“AISC”) per silver ounce sold averaged $29.58, $26.40 and $39.16, respectively.


- **Net loss** of $5.6 million for Q3-2026 (net loss of $16.5 million for Q3-2025) primarily attributable to higher net revenue and no loss on metals contract liabilities (following their settlement in Q2 2026), offset by higher loss on derivatives, and higher income tax expense.
- **Adjusted loss1** for Q3-2026 was $4.9 million or $0.02 per share (adjusted loss for Q3-2025 was $4.3 million or $0.06 per share) and **Adjusted EBITDA1** for Q3-2026 was $9.3 million or $0.03 per share (adjusted EBITDA for Q3-2025 was $1.9 million or $0.01 per share) primarily due to higher net revenue from increased realized silver prices during the period.


Paul Andre Huet, Chairman and CEO, commented: “I am very pleased to congratulate our operating team for their exemplary safety performance, having maintained a record of zero lost time accidents at our Galena Complex and Cosalá operations since March 2025 and April 2025, respectively. This achievement is not something we take for granted at Americas: to achieve a strong safety culture is always of the utmost importance and takes a significant effort from our entire operations and safety teams as we continue to implement our aggressive growth plans across the Company.


Operationally, our team delivered an exceptional third quarter, highlighted by record quarterly silver production and sales, a 68% increase in revenue to $51.4 million, and continued progress executing our growth strategy across both Galena and Cosalá. We produced over 800,000 ounces of silver during the quarter which represents a record quarter for Americas Gold and Silver in its 28-year history – a tremendous accomplishment. These results reflect the hard work, dedication, and operational discipline of our workforce, who continue to deliver strong performance while advancing multiple strategic initiatives across the business.


At Cosalá, the team continues to exceed expectations, delivering approximately 416,000 ounces of silver during the quarter, a 28% increase over the prior year period. Strong grades and stable mining rates at EC120, our flagship operation, continue to demonstrate the quality of the orebody and the significant value creation potential embedded within the district. Commercial production at EC120 has transformed Cosalá into a high-margin operation and provides a strong foundation for future growth. Given our recent drilling and the exploration success across the property, I know there is further potential at this very important asset in our diversified portfolio.


At Galena, we continued to build momentum on our multi-year revitalization plan. This plan involves a significant number of simultaneous capital projects, efficiency and optimization studies, communications upgrades and muck-moving improvements. As with all major multi-year mine improvement programs, these concurrent and iterative improvement efforts are interdependent and require a sequential approach, reanalysis and subsequent execution. Given the multi-faceted scope of these concurrent projects, I am extremely pleased with our progress to date and look forward to scaling this operation into a very significant silver, antimony, copper and lead mine in the years ahead.


With significant improvements made in hoisting capabilities, we have begun accelerating our waste development ahead of key production areas which is a critical step in setting up additional future long-hole panels. Our transition to increased long-hole mining in silver-copper zones relies on this waste development. Importantly, higher silver prices and the exceptional performance of Cosalá has allowed us to push waste development while remaining on track to deliver our 2026 consolidated production guidance.


Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we expect to achieve the lower end of our targeted 2026 production guidance of 3.2 to 3.6 million ounces of silver. With a September 30, 2026 cash balance of $63.3 million and potential total available liquidity of $113 million, a strengthened balance sheet following the settlement of our remaining precious metals delivery obligations, we are well positioned to execute on our growth plans. Overall, we continue to leverage the strength in silver markets to advance our significant objective of becoming one of North America’s leading silver producers and a strategic supplier of critical minerals.”


**Consolidated Production**


Consolidated silver production of 800,458 ounces during Q3-2026 was higher than Q3-2025 production of 764,757 ounces due to higher production Cosalá Operations partially offset by slightly lower production at Galena. Year-to-date Q3-2026 silver production was 2.3 million ounces, compared to the Company’s full year guidance of 3.2 to 3.6 million ounces.


Consolidated attributable cash costs and AISC for Q3-2026 were $29.66 per silver ounce and $42.94 per silver ounce, respectively. Year-to-date Q3-2026 silver cash costs and AISC were $26.40 per silver ounce and $39.16 per silver ounce, respectively.


**Galena Complex**


The Galena Complex produced 384,579 ounces of silver in Q3-2026 compared to 439,580 ounces of silver in Q3-2025 partially due to the impact of continued recovery from temporary operational interruptions experienced during the second quarter. The mine also produced 964,551 pounds of lead in Q3-2026 along with 182,362 pounds of copper and 101,011 pounds of antimony. Lead by-product production levels may vary in the short term as mining activities focus on increasing higher silver grade, tetrahedrite ore and supporting development continues to be advanced. Cash costs per ounce of silver sold increased to $44.31/oz in Q3-2026 from $25.10/oz in Q3-2025, primarily due to an increase in contractor expenses driving a significant number of concurrent projects underway.


During Q3-2026, the Company advanced several key operational initiatives at the Galena Complex, maintaining alignment with its multi year growth plan. Progress continued across underground development, long hole stoping, fleet modernization, shaft infrastructure upgrades, and communications improvements. These activities collectively support the Company’s objective of increasing mining efficiency, expanding production optionality, and improving long-term asset reliability.


Underground development advanced at a steady pace, supported by improved muck handling efficiencies. A significant contributor to these gains was the successful execution of the long-hole improvement plan at the Galena Complex. Remote mucking operations have materially outperformed traditional underhand and overhand methods, averaging approximately 200 tonnes per shift versus roughly 50 tonnes per shift historically. Long hole panels have achieved planned widths, reinforcing the decision to implement the long hole mining approach. Additional long hole stopes are currently in development for extraction in Q4 2026 and into 2027, further scaling production consistency and cost performance.


Development of the 55 179 decline is now ahead of the 55 198 and 55 206 stopes, enabling continued production during the quarter. The strategic location of this ramp provides access to multiple stopes from a single development heading, reducing future development expenditures and increasing operational flexibility. Two of the three stopes accessed from this ramp are planned for long hole mining, marking a notable transition given that no long hole stopes were active at year-end 2024.


**Cosalá Operations**


Silver production increased in Q3-2026 by 28% to 415,879 ounces of silver compared to 325,177 ounces of silver in Q3-2025, primarily due to higher silver grades during the period. Effective January 1, 2026, commercial production was declared for EC120, which has higher silver grades and recoveries based on its mineralogy compared to the zinc-lead-silver San Rafael mine orebody. Within mining focused in EC 120, copper production increased in Q3-2026 by 30% to 736,094 pounds compared to 565,707 pounds in Q3-2025. Mining has ceased at the San Rafael Main Central orebody which has removed zinc and lead production in 2026, although mining continues in the higher-grade silver Upper Zone orebody.


The recent Cosalá drilling results announced on September 17, 2026 returned exceptional results including 20.5 meters (true width) grading 654.7 g/t Ag and 1.5% Cu from hole SR583 in the San Rafael Upper Zone and intercepts of 14.1 meters (true width) grading 409.3 g/t Ag and 0.8% Cu, and 2.0 meters (true width) grading 754.9 g/t Ag and 0.5% Cu. Mineral Resource conversion drilling at the San Rafael Upper and 120 zones is consistently averaging 2-3x the previously reported inferred Mineral Resource grades (see Americas news release dated March 30, 2026) and represents significant upside potential that will be evaluated for mining in second half of 2027. In addition, Cosalá has strong exploration potential with little prior exploration drilling beyond the Mineral Resource zones.


Cash costs per silver ounce sold decreased during Q3-2026 to $14.51 per ounce from $24.79 per ounce in Q3-2025, due primarily to higher revenue from by-product credits recognized during the period.


**Outlook**


Americas’ consolidated production guidance for 2026 is a range between 3.2 million and 3.6 million ounces of silver at an AISC range of $30 to $35 per ounce sold. The Company expects to deliver towards the lower end of the production range and higher end of AISC guidance range.

**About Americas Gold and Silver Corporation**


Americas Gold and Silver Corporation is a rapidly growing North American producer of silver and other critical minerals supporting the growth of AI, electrification, advanced manufacturing, and national security. The Company owns a portfolio of high-grade mining assets in the United States and Mexico and is executing a strategy to become one of North America’s leading silver producers while establishing a secure domestic supply of antimony.


The Company’s flagship Galena Complex in Idaho is one of the United States' premier silver mining districts and includes the nation's largest antimony mine. Nearby, the fully permitted Crescent Silver Mine hosts one of the world's highest-grade silver resources and offers significant future growth potential through shared infrastructure and processing. Through a 51/49 joint venture, the Company is developing a fully integrated domestic antimony supply chain—from mine to finished product—to help strengthen America's critical mineral independence.


Americas also owns and operates the Cosalá Operations in Sinaloa, Mexico. With a strong balance sheet and multiple high-quality growth projects, the Company is well positioned to increase silver and antimony production while supplying the critical minerals needed to support the next generation of AI infrastructure, energy systems, and advanced industrial technologies.

*Average Realized Silver, Copper, Lead, Zinc and Antimony Prices*


The Company uses the financial measures ”average realized price“ because it understands that in addition to conventional measures prepared in accordance with IFRS, certain investors and analysts use this information to evaluate the Company’s performance vis-à-vis average market prices of metals for the period. The presentation of average realized metal prices is not meant to be a substitute for the revenue information presented in accordance with IFRS, but rather should be evaluated in conjunction with such IFRS measure.


Average realized metal prices represent the sale price of the underlying metal excluding unrealized mark-to-market gains and losses on provisional pricing and concentrate treatment and refining charges. Average realized silver, copper, lead, zinc and antimony prices are calculated as the revenue related to each of the metals sold, e.g. revenue from sales of silver divided by the quantity of ounces sold.

*Cash Costs and Cash Costs/Ag Oz Sold*


The Company uses the financial measures “Cash Costs” and “Cash Costs/Ag Oz Sold” in accordance with measures widely reported in the silver mining industry, as developed by the World Gold Council, as a benchmark for performance measurement and because it understands that, in addition to conventional measures prepared in accordance with IFRS, certain investors and analysts use this information to evaluate the Company’s underlying cash costs of operations. *EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, and Adjusted Earnings*


The Company uses the financial measures “EBITDA”, “adjusted EBITDA” and “adjusted earnings” as indicators of the Company’s ability to generate operating cash flows to fund working capital needs, service debt obligations, and fund exploration and evaluation, and capital expenditures. These financial measures exclude the impact of certain items and therefore is not necessarily indicative of operating profit or cash flows from operating activities as determined under IFRS. Other companies may calculate these financial measures differently. Additional details regarding weighted average number of common shares outstanding are disclosed in Notes 16 to the Company’s condensed interim consolidated financial statements.


EBITDA is net income (loss) under IFRS before depletion and amortization, interest and financing expense, and income taxes. Adjusted EBITDA further excludes other non-cash items such as accretion expenses, impairment charges, and other fair value gains and losses.
